The Argument You Would Have Been Weighing On Oscar Health

The shares cost US$14.37 at the start of the period, so any buyer had to decide whether Oscar Health’s AI story could justify a much higher price or not.

The opposing case saw analysts assigning a fair value of US$11.29, with the key worry that higher claims costs, policy shifts and changing risk pools could pressure profitability even if digital adoption and new healthcare initiatives gained traction.

Oscar Health’s Q3 2026 figures, with revenue of US$5.14b and net income of US$167.3m compared with a Q3 2025 loss of US$137.5m, leaned toward the optimistic case that assumed margin progress. Net margin moved from a 4.6% loss to a 3.3% profit. Insider selling and ongoing regulatory risks from the news flow kept the cautious case alive, so the evidence cut both ways.

The key lesson is simple. When a story rests on AI driven efficiency and new platforms, treat operating margin and reported medical loss ratios as the scorecard, and check whether each quarter moves those lines in the direction the pitch implied.
